title: The Enlightenment
key_facts: Intellectual movement advancing reason, natural rights, and skepticism of traditional authority
Salons, encyclopedias, and republics of letters spread ideas across borders
Critiques of absolutism and church dominance informed reform and revolution
causes: Printing press and expanding reading publics
Cross‑cultural exchange through exploration and commerce
outcome: Codification of political philosophy (separation of powers, social contract)
Educational, legal, and religious reforms; toleration debates
Influence on the American and French Revolutions
impacts: Blueprints for constitutional government and civil liberties
Secularization of learning and growth of public sphere
Catalyst for Atlantic revolutions and modern institutions
